item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Thursday
item.description: Almost half of shop owners victims of crime last year, majority of Swedes want politicians to tackle climate change, more than usual sought help at Christmas and more news from Sweden on Thursday.

item.title: Most Swedes want government action on climate change
item.description: A WWF survey released on January 29th shows that an increasing number of Swedes think that responsibility for addressing climate and environmental issues lies with governments, not individuals.

item.title: EU announces new push to overhaul visa system and deportations policy
item.description: The European Union on Thursday laid out plans to overhaul its visa system and step up deportations as part of a five-year migration strategy that cements a hardening line on the hot-button issue.

item.title: Why hasn't Sweden joined the euro and will it ever happen?
item.description: Despite joining the EU in 1994, Sweden still hasn’t joined the euro. Why is this, and could it ever happen in the future?

item.title: What do we know about the Sweden Democrat MP under investigation for drunk driving?
item.description: SD Member of Parliament Katja Nyberg, a former police officer who has been the party spokesperson for police issues, was stopped for suspected drunk driving over the holidays. Blood tests have now come back positive for both alcohol and narcotics.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: vagn
item.description: This word of the day translates easily to English as ‘wagon’, but its wide use in compound words makes it a great Swedish word to have in your vocabulary.

item.title: Sweden's government asks Migration Agency to propose exemptions to work permit law
item.description: Sweden's government has ordered the Migration Agency to draw up a list of in demand professions which will be exempted from the new higher salary requirement set to come into force later this year.

item.title: EU announces plan to extend 90-day rule for certain non-EU workers
item.description: The European Commission has announced it will look into allowing certain non-EU professionals to stay in the EU beyond the current 90-day rule, as part of a future overall of its visa system. It also asked EU countries to make visa access "simpler and faster" for skilled workers.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Friday
item.description: Sweden Democrat MP suspected of drunk driving goes independent, new grading system delayed by a year, politicians cleared of charges after refusing to accept refugees and other news from Sweden on Friday.

item.title: Sweden denies Turkey request to hear journalist facing terror charges
item.description: Sweden's government said on Thursday that it was denying a request from Turkey for a Swedish court to interrogate a journalist facing terror charges in Turkey.
